# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I have no established gesture vocabulary, so I should start conveying the bomb's visible info to Blind via speech (Blind can hear me), and gesture something simple to Mute to acknowledge.

Let me report the raw facts to Blind first, since Blind can act and needs my visual data most.

```
speak(to="blind", text="display shows 7. light is yellow. strip painted blue red red, three stripes. keypad engraved 1 is 6, 2 is 8, 3 is 7, 4 is 0, it wants 1 digit entered, nothing entered yet. wires in order: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white.")

```

The display changed from 7 to 6, and light changed from yellow to red - these seem to update each turn, possibly a countdown or a state that matters for the manual's instructions. So gestures are the only way Mute can reach me directly.

I need to keep feeding Blind the live visual state since it seems to change turn by turn, and try to build a simple gesture protocol with Mute since I can't ask questions via speech to Mute (Mute can't hear me speak either - only Blind can hear me). Actually let me check: my speak goes to Mute and Blind both (they can hear). So Mute CAN hear my speech. Good - I can talk to Mute via speech.

Let me ask Mute what the manual needs, and continue relaying board state to Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="display now shows 6, light is red, changed from before. strip still blue red red. keypad still 1:6 2:8 3:7 4:0 wants 1 digit. wires unchanged 1 blue 2 yellow 3 orange 4 red 5 purple 6 white. does the manual need the display number, light color, strip colors, keypad digit, or a wire color? gesture back which one matters most using pointing or numbers if you can.")

Mute speaks first, I should receive Mute's speech since Mute can speak to me... wait, "Mute" cannot speak at all per role table: "Mute: Read the manual / Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." So Mute can NEVER speak - only gesture. That's why Mute only gestures to me.

So I can't get info from Mute except gestures, and gestures alone (without an established code) can't carry rich info. But Blind can speak (no restriction on Blind speaking), and Blind can hear me. So the real channel is: I feed Blind visual info via speech, Blind can hear Mute's... no wait, Mute can't speak. So Blind must get manual info from Mute via speech - but Mute can't speak either. Let me re-check: Blind's restrictions: "Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." Blind can hear and speak presumably (not restricted). Mute cannot speak - only gesture, which Blind cannot see. So Mute and Blind cannot communicate directly at all except through me relaying.

So I'm the hub. I see gestures from Mute, I can speak to both Blind and Mute. I need to relay: I gesture is one-way FROM Mute TO me only. I cannot gesture back understanding easily, but I could speak to Mute (Mute can hear). Let me set up a numeric gesture code with Mute: numbers via finger-count.

```
speak(to="mute", text="i cannot tell what your gestures mean yet. let's use fingers as numbers: hold up 1 finger for display, 2 for light, 3 for strip, 4 for keypad, 5 for wires, to tell me which one the manual cares about first. i will then ask yes or no questions and you gesture thumbs up for yes thumbs down for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="display now 7, light now blue. strip blue red red unchanged. keypad 1:6 2:8 3:7 4:0 wants 1 digit, none entered. wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 orange 4 red 5 purple 6 white unchanged. mute cannot speak, only gesture to me, so i am setting up a number code with mute to find out what the manual needs.")
```
